sections.h2: Where is Lake County, Indiana, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Lake County is the Indiana county in the far northwest corner of the state, on the Lake Michigan shore and inside the Chicago metro area. Crown Point is the county seat. The county covers 626.5 square miles, of which 498.9 is land and 127.6 is water, which gives it more water area than any of Indiana's 92 counties.

Lake County was established on February 16, 1837. Its land is flat in the north and south, with the Valparaiso Moraine rising through the middle. The lowest point is 585 feet on the lake shoreline and the highest is 801 feet in northeastern Winfield Township. Porter County lies to the east, Jasper and Newton counties to the south, and Cook, Will and Kankakee counties in Illinois to the west.

The county has 19 incorporated places. Hammond is the largest by population at 77,879, and Gary is the largest by area. Calumet Township is the most populous township, with 91,970 residents in 2020.

sections.h2: How did steel shape Lake County's economy and housing?
sections.html:
Heavy industry built most of Lake County's older neighborhoods. Inland Steel opened a plant in East Chicago in 1903, and U.S. Steel founded Gary Works in 1906. Population climbed from 37,892 in 1900 to 261,310 in 1930 and peaked at 546,253 in 1970.

Steel employment topped 60,000 in the 1960s and fell to about 18,000 by 2015. The 2020 census count of 498,700 is well below that peak. Gary Works employed over 30,000 people in 1970 and 2,246 in 2023, and Gary's 2020 census found 23.2% of its housing units vacant.

Industry still matters. The employers Wikipedia lists include U.S. Steel Gary Works, Cleveland-Cliffs Indiana Harbor Works in East Chicago, the BP Whiting Refinery, Canadian National Railway and Unilever in Whiting, Cargill in Hammond and NiSource in Merrillville. In 2010, manufacturing was the largest employment sector at over 45,000 workers, followed by health care and social assistance at 44,000 and public administration at 40,000.

The result is a county with very different housing stock from one block to the next. Gary's vacancy rate and Crown Point's steady growth sit in the same county and on the same tax rolls. Owners of inherited or damaged houses in the older parts of the county are often the ones who ask about as-is sales.

sections.h2: What is each Lake County city known for?
sections.html:
• Hammond: 77,879 residents in 2020, an industrial city that borders Chicago and Lake Michigan. The School City of Hammond runs 11 elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools.
  • Gary: 69,093 residents in 2020, down from 178,320 in 1960. It is the western gateway to Indiana Dunes National Park and has Gary/Chicago International Airport.
  • Crown Point: 33,899 residents in 2020. Center Township is served by Crown Point Community School Corporation and Ross Township by Merrillville Community School Corporation. The Lake County Fair is held there each August.

The Lake County school district a house sits in feeds directly into its tax rate, which is why the same assessed value can produce different bills in Hammond, Gary and Crown Point.

sections.h2: What is the weather in Lake County, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Lake County has cold, snowy winters and warm summers. At the Lowell weather station, normals from 1981 to 2010 show 39.46 inches of precipitation and 29.3 inches of snow a year, with a January average low of 14.4 degrees and a July average high of 83.8 degrees. The record low is minus 29 in December 1989 and the record high is 104 in June 1988.

Lake-effect snow adds to winter totals near the shore, and thunderstorms occur on about 40 to 50 days a year. Freeze and thaw cycles are hard on roofs, gutters and old plumbing, and houses with deferred maintenance tend to show it. A cash sale lets the owner skip repairs that a mortgage buyer might demand.

sections.h2: How do roads and trains connect Lake County?
sections.html:
Interstate 65 runs north and south through the county, and the Frank Borman Expressway (I-80/94 with US 6) links the Illinois line to the Indiana Toll Road. US 30 follows the old Lincoln Highway, US 12 east of Gary is the Dunes Highway, and Broadway (IN 53) and Cline Avenue (IN 912) fill in the grid.

The South Shore Line commuter rail serves the county, and the Munster/Dyer station opened on March 31, 2026. About 44,000 workers commuted from Lake County to Chicago in 2007.

sections.h2: Which Lake County office do I contact about property tax?
sections.html:
The county treasurer has three counter locations, each open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Auditor's office is in the Crown Point government building.

sections.h2: Why are Lake County's 2026 assessment notices different?
sections.html:
For 2026, the state lists no Form 11 mailing in Calumet, Center, Hobart, Ross and St. John townships, and it shows a June 15, 2027 appeal deadline for them. That is a year later than the June 15, 2026 deadline listed for LaPorte County.

Each of those townships has its own assessor line: Calumet (219) 885-0555, Center (219) 663-0841, Hobart (219) 942-7878, Ross (219) 769-7667 and St. John (219) 365-2777. If your house is in another Lake County township, call the county number to find out which notice applies. When no Form 11 is sent, the state says the tax bill serves as the notice.

sections.h2: How does Indiana's 2025 property tax law affect Lake County owners?
sections.html:
Homestead owners in Lake County get a $48,000 standard deduction on taxes payable in 2026, which drops to $40,000 for 2027 and $30,000 for 2028. In exchange, the supplemental deduction rises from 40% to 46% to 52% over the same years. A new credit gives homesteads that qualify for the standard deduction the lesser of 10% of their liability or $300 without an application.

The old over-65 deduction became a credit of up to $150, with income limits of $60,000 single and $70,000 joint. Caps stay at 1% of gross assessed value for homesteads, 2% for other residential and farm land, and 3% for other property. Lake County's Auditor links to an online deduction filing page for these claims.

sections.h2: What is the Lake County tax sale and can an owner stop it?
sections.html:
Yes, an owner can stop a sale, but only by paying before the deadline. The 2026 Lake County tax sale ran online at zeusauction.com beginning at 5:30 p.m. on September 4, 2026, and properties started closing in batches on September 7.

  • To pull a parcel from the sale, the Treasurer had to receive the amount due by 4:30 p.m. on September 4, in cash or certified funds
  • Postmarks did not count, and payment had to arrive by mail or in person at 2293 N. Main Street
  • The minimum bid covered delinquent taxes, special assessments, current-year taxes, penalties and a $50 postage and publication amount, plus other sale costs
  • Owners of record may have a right to surplus if a parcel sold above the minimum bid and is not redeemed

Redemption for certificates sold in 2026 expires September 8, 2027. The cost is 110% of the minimum bid within six months of the sale and 115% after that, plus any excess bid with 5% annual interest. Anyone who owns a parcel that sold should read the county's tax sale notice now.

sections.h2: How does selling a Lake County house with tax due work?
sections.html:
Taxes are paid in two installments, with the state listing May 11 and November 10 for 2026, and a payment made within 30 days late, by an owner with no earlier delinquency, carries a 5% penalty while later payment costs 10%. A seller who is behind can sell before a sale is scheduled and have the balance paid from the closing proceeds.

Appeals follow the state path. File Form 130 with the assessing official, expect an informal meeting, and then a hearing by the county board within 180 days. If you disagree, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review. Only the current assessment can be appealed this way, and evidence can be a sale, comparable sales or an appraisal.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The state lists May 11 and November 10 as the 2026 due dates. Payments go to the county treasurer.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Lake County property tax in person?
faqs.a: You can pay at the Treasurer's offices in Crown Point, Hammond or Gary, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Did Lake County send assessment notices in 2026?
faqs.a: Not in every township. The state shows no Form 11 mailed for Calumet, Center, Hobart, Ross and St. John, with a June 15, 2027 appeal date.

faqs.q: How can I find out if my Lake County parcel is in a tax sale?
faqs.a: Check the Treasurer's tax sale list, or call 219-755-3760. The county posts its notice, parcel list and eligibility details on the Treasurer's page.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lake County house before it goes to a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, if the closing happens before the deadline to remove the parcel. The balance can be paid from the proceeds, so call early.
